name: Carlos Calderon
event: UFC Fight Night: Cortes-Acosta vs. Walker
summary: Carlos 'The Chief' Calderon (11-4, 1 NC, age 31) is the reigning Fury FC featherweight champion. He makes his UFC debut against Austin Bashi on four days' notice after Lucas Brennan tore his ACL. He is a submission-first finisher: six of his 11 wins are submissions, two more are R1 KOs, and he is on a three-fight win streak (5-1 in his last six). He won the Fury belt by R4 rear-naked choke over UFC veteran Damon Jackson in May and defended it over five rounds against Lorram Esteves on Oct 2. His one step up to UFC-level opposition was a 2024 Contender Series loss, a R2 anaconda choke by Alberto Montes, also taken on short notice.

how_they_fight.Striking: A volume striker who starts fast (Cageside Press, 2024), but that breakdown was harsh on the craft: low hands, 'leads in with his chin', sloppy and reckless entries. On the Contender Series he threw a lot (37 of 88 significant, 42%) while Montes landed 38 of 57; UFC.com said Calderon 'showed a varied offense' in a fast first round. His two KO wins were both in R1 and very fast (0:17 and 0:25, 2022), against regional opposition.
how_they_fight.Grappling: This is the main weapon. Six submission wins: R1 x3 (Ellis 2024, Alvarez 2025, Torres 2026), R2 x1 (Gavidia 2023), R3 x1 (Broadwater 2021, at 4:59) and R4 x1 (Jackson, RNC, 2:07). ClutchPoints says he threatens to take the back and finish. Cageside (2024) said he 'can snatch up the neck if his opponent is lazy', but rated his position and takedown defense poorly. He landed 2 of 6 takedowns and had about 2:39 of control against Montes.
how_they_fight.Defense: The 2024 Cageside breakdown called his defense 'terrible all around', and that was before the Fury FC title run. His four losses: two submissions (Motaz Askar R1, 2022; Montes R2, 2024 anaconda choke after a takedown) and two decisions (Elijah Leggett 2023, Mauricio Gomez split 2025). Never stopped by strikes in our data. Both submission losses came against grapplers who got on top of him.
how_they_fight.Pace & cardio: Went deep twice in 2026: a R4 finish of Jackson and a full 25-minute decision over Esteves. He has three decision wins (two of them split or five-round) and finishes spread across R1-R4. Cardio over 15 minutes shouldn't be a problem. He fought five weeks ago, so ClutchPoints argued the short-notice weight cut was not a concern; he made 145.5 at the weigh-ins.
how_they_fight.Fight IQ: Took both of his biggest opportunities (Contender Series and now the UFC) on short notice. Has beaten one UFC veteran (Damon Jackson) and nobody else of note; Cageside said in 2024 the best record he had beaten was 4-3.

patterns: Submission finisher: 6 of 11 wins by submission, back-taking and chokes
Fast starter: 5 of 8 finishes in R1
Two five-round fights in 2026, both wins
Short-notice UFC debut; a big betting underdog (+400 per DraftKings, via ClutchPoints)
concerns: Defense and hand position (Cageside, 2024); untested against UFC strikers
Taken down and submitted by both UFC-calibre opponents he has faced (Montes; Bashi in 67 seconds)
Thin evidence: no tracked stats beyond one 2024 bout, and nothing recent describes his style in detail
Short notice: four days, after a fight five weeks earlier
keys_to_beat: Wrestle him: Montes took him down in R2 and finished from top
Avoid giving him the back in scrambles
Make him strike defensively; Cageside rated his defense poorly

news.text: Made weight at the official weigh-ins: 145.5 lb (Bashi also 145.5).
Signed to replace Lucas Brennan (torn ACL) against Austin Bashi at featherweight, on four days' notice; UFC debut. Heavy.com first reported it; MMA Fighting's Mike Heck confirmed.
Was originally scheduled to defend his Fury FC title in the Fury FC 127 main event on Jan 15.
DraftKings odds via ClutchPoints: Bashi -535, Calderon +400; ClutchPoints picks Bashi inside 2.5 rounds.
Defended the Fury FC featherweight title with a five-round unanimous decision over Lorram Esteves.
Won the Fury FC featherweight title by R4 rear-naked choke over Damon Jackson.
Submitted by Alberto Montes (anaconda choke, 2:38 R2) on the Contender Series after Montes took him down; Montes got the contract.
Submitted by Austin Bashi (rear-naked choke) at 1:07 of R1 in his short-notice UFC debut: taken down after a wild exchange, his guillotine failed and Bashi took his back.
